components.gap: Relational and typed Henkin/general completeness are supplied, and the reader distinguishes them from full semantics (second-and-higher-order-logic-supplement.tex:259-300; second-and-higher-order-logic-w02-p02-040.tex:1202-1214, 1465-1469). The nonaxiomatizability side is not cleanly supplied, however. The theorem the reader points to, thm:p02-w02-p02-040-no-effective-calculus (040 body 1443-1459), is marked proved= for all five clauses. Yet the handbook's own boundary (second-and-higher-order-logic-w02b-p02-034.tex:83-99, 422-427) says clause 1's decidability assertion is unproved: it rests on the computability of primitive recursive functions, which is given only as an outline. The restoration paragraph (inherited-12415-12536.tex:35-37, 51-53) also says the computability step through thm:p04-ce-sigma-one is proved in 040, although that theorem is marked sketched= (decision-problems-and-arithmetical-hierarchy.tex:330). Both present an unproved dependency as proved, which is the failure condition. Complete proofs of clauses 3-5 exist only in the 034 section, and neither the 040 theorem nor the restoration routes to them. Separately, the imported typed completeness theorems for Henkin's own system remain cited (inherited-12537-12673.tex:36-48; inherited-12784-12923.tex:58-67). Henkin1950 is not held (spec/coverage/edition-2026/held-sources.json), so it cannot be confirmed that the Church general-model completeness (040 body 1155-1173) discharges those imported obligations. Uncertainty is not coverage.
